dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Looking for somewhere to eat your fill and sleep soundly? Then you've come to the right place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What would you recommend?

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Here's the menu.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, you are...

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: I'm the owner of the Weary Inn, and I also run a food stall at the entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Speaking of this place, I even stayed here for free back when I was a contestant. Who'd have thought I'd be the one in charge now, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Do you know anyone who's taken part in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame?

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: If you did, that would make things a lot easier. You could stay with them, and you'd dine and bunk on the house — all you can eat, too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Feel free to come back anytime.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How have things been lately?

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Thanks for asking. Things have been going fine.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Many old comrades have stopped by for meals since the battles ended. Though each of them still nurses injuries of their own, they all seem quite happy.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: ...Of course, it's possible that it's all just a front, and that they're hiding their discontent from me.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Thanks to my old injuries, however, I can't really help them out anymore. The best I can do is treat them to a few more meals.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How have things been lately?

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Thanks for asking. Things have been going great.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Many old comrades have stopped by for meals since the battles ended. Though each of them still nurses injuries of their own, they all seem quite happy.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: ...Of course, it's possible that it's all just a front, and that they're hiding any unhappiness from me.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: We all know how the joy of peace and the pain of loss can coexist. I just hope they can come here often. They can eat and drink on the house!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Any recommendations?

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Well, I'd go with my personal specialty, Tatacos.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: That said, though, it's not hard to make. Almost everyone in Natlan knows how.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Here, hold out your hand.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Hehe, were you expecting me to just give you finished product? Nah, I'm going to teach you how to make one!
